issues: Categories backup and restore tests are failing: hidden flag is not persisted correctly. In src/lib/categories.ts, custom categories are stored with a 'hidden' flag only in the hidden array, but getAllCategories does not expose the hidden flag on returned objects, causing hidden property undefined in tests. The test expects hiddenCat.hidden to be true, but hiddenCat.hidden is undefined. Fix by including hidden property in getAllCategories return objects (already present) and ensure hideCategory sets hidden flag correctly for custom categories, and that restoreBackup correctly restores hidden state. Also ensure renameCategory and hideCategory maintain hidden flag after backup/restore.

OCR test is passing but the acceptance test m6 fails with an error in src/lib/ocr.ts: getInfoAsync from expo-file-system throws a deprecation warning error due to using legacy method. recognizeReceiptText uses FileSystem.getInfoAsync which is the new API and should work, but the stack trace shows getInfoAsync from expo-file-system/legacyWarnings.ts causing an error "Method getInfoAsync imported from \"expo-file-system\" is deprecated". The mock for expo-file-system likely does not provide getInfoAsync, leading to the warning being treated as an error and causing test failure. Provide a mock implementation for expo-file-system.getInfoAsync (or adjust recognizeReceiptText to use the new FileSystem API without triggering legacy warnings) to prevent the error.

Category deletion protection test expects deleteCategory to return an error when the category is in use, but the test uses deleteCategory which is not exported from src/lib/categories.ts (the function is defined but not exported). Ensure deleteCategory is exported in src/lib/categories.ts so the test can call it, or update the test to use the correct exported function.
feedback: Fix the hidden flag handling in categories, provide a proper mock for expo-file-system getInfoAsync to avoid legacy warning errors, and export deleteCategory (or adjust the test) so the categories tests pass. Once these issues are corrected, re-run the test suite.
